label: late original-phase tokens in q/c/l/w-initial sequences (no clean rule)
explanation: Very sparse (0.012% of steps) weak feature (max 0.23). 93% of mass is in the original phase at t>=4, mostly the last 1-3 tokens before <DEL>, plus some on <DEL> itself; it essentially never fires during the copy phase or at t<3. Sequences starting with q (15x lift), c, l or w hold ~98% of mass; enriched current inputs are v (9x), 3, f, and enriched previous inputs are h, j, u. These factors combine only loosely: the context envelope (original phase, t>=3, first token q/c/l/w) covers 91% of mass at 0.3% precision, and the tightest conjunction (with in_tok v/f/3 and prev h/j/u) reaches only ~10-16% precision at ~20% recall (dev F1 0.14). It looks like it fires on a particular rare hidden-state combination, not on a nameable token or position rule. Magnitude rises mildly with in_tok v and first token q (top examples are almost all q...v), but I did not find a predictor of magnitude beyond that.
